bert.description: BERT-base-uncased already fine-tuned on SST-2 by TextAttack; used frozen, no new training

label_mapping_fallback.source: The checkpoint config only contains generic id2label names (LABEL_0/LABEL_1). The mapping index 0=NEG, index 1=POS is the GLUE SST-2 convention, was verified by ../bert_shap/VERIFICATION.md (10/10 S1-S10) and ../clip_text_shap_improved Part 7 (bert_label_mapping in part7_checks.json), and is re-verified here on the independent S1-S10 sentences below before any scoring of the evaluation set.

clip.description: Frozen CLIP ViT-B/32 text encoder used zero-shot with NEG/POS prompt prototypes; no classification head is trained
clip.prompt_selection_note: Selected in clip_text_shap_improved Part 2 on the internal prompt-validation split (6,735 SST-2 training sentences); selection_uses_final_evaluation=false.

NEG: This film left a bad impression.
I would not recommend this film.

shap.masking: whole-word deletion (mask_token='', collapse_mask_token=True) followed by re-tokenization

tolerances.rationale: Float32 model outputs. CLIP cosine similarities are O(0.2) and accumulate ~1e-7 kernel noise; BERT logits are O(4) so float32 round-off and batch-shape-dependent GPU kernels are ~10x larger. Batch-parity tolerances equal the additivity tolerances because both measure the same numerical source (re-evaluating one text under a different batch composition).
